items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S3445

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the labor law and the general business law, in
relation to the prompt payment of employees and contractors engaged in
private construction projects


 PURPOSE :
This bill amends New York's labor law and prompt pay law to ensure
greater enforcement mechanisms are available for employees,
contractors and subcontractors.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :
This bill amends Section 196-a of the labor law by adding a new
subdivision (ii) which allows an employee, contractor or certified
collective bargaining agent to complain to the commissioner of Labor
regarding a violation or potentially imminent violation of article 6
of the labor law.

This bill also amends 756 section (1) of the general business law by
lowering the aggregate cost threshold for private construction
projects from two hundred fifty thousand dollars to one hundred fifty
thousand dollars; lowering the aggregate size threshold for
residential construction projects from 9,000 square feet to 4,500
square feet or less; and lowering the size of applicable residential
public housing units from 150 to 75 units.

This bill amends 756-a section (1) by changing the billing cycle to be
the calendar month within which the work is performed.

This bill amends 756-b by allowing contractors the use of arbitration
as a permissive remedy for non-payment.

The bill amends 756b by adding a new section (3) that creates a system
of protocols for the use of arbitration in scenarios of non-payment.

This bill amends 757 by adding a new section (3) relating to the void
provisions of construction contracts and adding new language
pertaining to the use of arbitration.

 JUSTIFICATION :
This bill is necessary to ensure that Payments required by
construction contracts are made in a timely manner.  Failure to pay in
a timely manner often jeopardizes the operations of contractors,
subcontractors and material suppliers and places the wages, benefits
and jobs of employees at risk.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
2008 Session: A.11520 - John - reported to Codes Committee

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None.

 LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately and applies to construction contracts entered into after
the bill becomes law and for contract entered into prior to the
effective date for which permit or permits have been issued and work
has begun.
